civilServantPay.title: 2027 Korean Civil Servant Pay Table & Take-home Pay
civilServantPay.subtitle: Monthly base pay by grade and step for general, police/fire and teacher tracks in 2026, a 2027 estimate (+3.9% government proposal), and take-home pay after the civil service pension contribution, health insurance and tax.

y2027.title: 2027 estimate
y2027.note: The government's 2027 budget proposal raises civil service pay by {p}%. We multiply every cell of the 2026 table by that rate and round to the nearest ₩100. The confirmed table follows the National Assembly vote and the January amendment of the regulation. If junior grades 7-9 get an extra raise as in 2026, actual pay will be higher. Health and long-term care use 2027 rates; allowances use 2026 amounts.

detail.taxable: Taxable pay (basis for contributions and tax)
detail.localTax: Local income tax (10% of income tax)
detail.noNps: Civil servants pay the civil service pension instead of the National Pension and are not covered by employment insurance.

notes.base: Pension contributions and health premiums are normally based on last year's income. Here we approximate them with this month's taxable pay. The real basis includes bonuses and holiday allowances, so actual deductions are often higher.
notes.cap: The pension income cap (160% of the all-civil-servant average) is not applied because we could not confirm the 2026 amount from the official notice. It only matters for the highest steps of the top grades.
notes.excluded: Family allowance, overtime pay, the long-service add-on (₩30,000 a month under 5 years of service) and job-specific allowances vary by person and are not included.
notes.teacher: Classroom teachers are not listed in the position allowance table (Allowance Regulation, Table 15), so only the meal allowance is added.

whatIs.title: What is the civil servant pay table?
whatIs.description: The pay table sets the monthly base pay for each track in the Public Officials Remuneration Regulation. Within one table, the same grade and step means the same pay. A new table with that year's raise takes effect each January, and the Ministry of Personnel Management publishes it. This tool calculates take-home pay from the confirmed 2026 table and shows a 2027 estimate using the proposed 3.9% raise.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Pick a track (general, police/fire or teacher). Grade 9, step 1 of the general track is shown first.
Pick your grade and step. If you do not know your step, see 'How is the starting step set?' below.
Set the number of dependents (including yourself) and children aged 8-20 to apply the withholding tax table.
Turn off 'Include fixed monthly allowances' to calculate with base pay only.
Compare pay by step and starting pay for grades 9-5 in the tables, and copy the link to share the same settings.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Gross = base pay + meal allowance ₩160,000 + position allowance (₩175,000-₩750,000 by grade)
Taxable pay = gross − meal allowance (meal allowance is tax-free up to ₩200,000 a month)
Pension contribution = taxable pay × 9% (Public Officials Pension Act Art. 67)
Health insurance = taxable pay × 3.595%, long-term care = health premium × 13.14% (2026, amounts under ₩10 dropped)
Income tax = simplified withholding table (dependents and children aged 8-20), local income tax = income tax × 10%
2027 estimated pay = 2026 pay × 1.039, rounded to the nearest ₩100

realWorld.title: Why a pay slip may differ
items: Contribution and premium bases come from last year's income, so people with large bonuses and holiday allowances pay more than shown here.
Family allowance, overtime pay, the long-service add-on (from ₩30,000 a month under 5 years) and job-specific allowances are not included.
Gross pay and income tax jump in months with the long-service allowance (January, July) and holiday allowance (Lunar New Year, Chuseok).
Some offices also deduct association or union fees.

comparison.title: Civil service pension vs. National Pension
items: Civil servants contribute 9% of standard monthly income; the government also pays 9% of the pay budget.
Private employees pay 4.75% to the National Pension in 2026 and 5% in 2027, so the pension deduction is larger for civil servants on the same pay.
Civil servants are not covered by employment insurance, so there is no employment insurance premium.
Health and long-term care insurance use the same rates as private employees, split half and half with the government.

tips.title: Good to know
items: The 2027 table is confirmed only after the National Assembly passes the budget and the regulation is amended. We will replace the table then.
In 2026, pay rose 3.5% overall and starting pay for junior grades 7-9 rose an extra 3.1% (6.6% in total). Check the confirmed table for any extra raise in 2027.
Mandatory military service of up to 3 years counts toward your starting step.
The long-service allowance is paid in January and July: 10% (under 2 years) to 50% (10 years or more) of monthly base pay.

items.q: How is the starting step set?
items.a: General, police and fire officials with no recognized experience start at step 1 of their grade. If you only have mandatory military service, that period (up to 3 years) counts as years of service plus one. For example, 1 year 6 months of service gives step 2, and the remaining 6 months count toward the next step. Teachers start from a base step by certificate (grade-2 teacher 8, grade-1 teacher 9) plus education and experience adjustments, so a grade-2 teacher from a 4-year teacher-training program with no experience starts at step 9 (Remuneration Regulation Tables 15, 23, 25).

items.q: What is the difference between base pay and total pay?
items.a: Base pay is the monthly amount set in the pay table by grade and step. Total pay adds allowances: monthly ones such as the meal and position allowances, ones paid in set months such as the long-service and holiday allowances, and personal ones such as family allowance and overtime. The long-service and holiday allowances are percentages of base pay, so they rise with it.

items.q: How much more is the civil service pension contribution than the National Pension?
items.a: The civil service pension contribution is 9% of standard monthly income. Private employees pay 4.75% to the National Pension in 2026, so on ₩3,000,000 of taxable pay a civil servant pays ₩270,000 and a private employee ₩142,500. Civil servants do not pay employment insurance (0.9% for private employees).

items.q: Why is my result below the '₩3 million for grade 9 starters' headline?
items.a: The government figure is the monthly average of base pay plus all allowances before deductions. For 2026, total pay for grade 9, step 1 was announced at ₩34.28 million a year (₩2.86 million a month), while base pay is ₩2,133,000. Fixed monthly pay is ₩2,498,000: base pay plus the ₩160,000 meal allowance, ₩175,000 position allowance and ₩30,000 long-service add-on. The rest comes from allowances paid in set months, such as holiday and long-service allowances, spread over 12 months. Take-home pay is lower still after contributions, premiums and tax. The ₩3 million target for 2027 uses the same basis.

items.q: When are the long-service and holiday allowances paid?
items.a: The long-service allowance is paid on the January and July paydays: 10% (under 2 years) to 50% (10 years or more) of monthly base pay. The holiday allowance is 60% of monthly base pay at Lunar New Year and Chuseok for those in service. Neither is included in the monthly take-home pay here.

items.q: When will the 2027 pay table be confirmed?
items.a: The 2027 budget proposal approved by the Cabinet on 1 September 2026 includes a 3.9% raise. After the National Assembly passes the budget and the regulation is amended, the Ministry of Personnel Management publishes the new table. The 2026 table took effect on 1 January. The 2027 figures here apply 3.9% to every cell and will be replaced by the confirmed table.

items.q: Can I see the military pay table?
items.a: The military table (Remuneration Regulation Table 13) uses different ranks, steps and allowances, so it is not included yet. We plan to add it in January with the confirmed 2027 tables.

items.q: Do civil servants pay employment insurance or the National Pension?
items.a: Neither. National and local civil servants are excluded from the Employment Insurance Act (special and fixed-term officials may opt in to unemployment benefits), and they pay the civil service pension instead of the National Pension. Health and long-term care insurance use the same rates as private employees.
